action.action-desc: Mr. Gottheimer introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Financial Services

form.official-title: To amend the Federal Deposit Insurance Act to make changes to the Standard Maximum Deposit Insurance Amount, and for other purposes.

subsection.text: Section 11(a) of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act (12 U.S.C. 1821(a)) is amended—

subparagraph.text: by striking after March 31, 2010 and all that follows through to the end of subparagraph (E); and

paragraph.text: by striking subparagraph (F) and inserting the following:

subparagraph.text: On January 1 of the year following the year during which this subparagraph was enacted, and each January 1 thereafter, the Corporation shall—

clause.text: adjust the first dollar figure described in subparagraph (E) by a percentage equal to the percentage increase, if any, in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics for the most recent 12-month period for which data are available; and
round each adjusted dollar figure down to the nearest $10,000.

subsection.text: The amendments made by this section shall take effect 180 days after the date of the enactment of this section.

The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation and the National Credit Union Administration shall jointly, not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this section, submit a report to the Congress after conducting research and analysis that determines the appropriate amount for the standard maximum deposit insurance amount under section 11(A)(1)(E) of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act.

When determining the appropriate amount for the standard maximum deposit insurance amount under section 11(A)(1)(E) of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation and the National Credit Union Administration shall consider the amounts of assets held by institutions, the distribution of deposit balances across institutions, the ratio between insured and uninsured deposits, and effects on the Deposit Insurance Fund.
The report submitted by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation and the National Credit Union Administration under subsection (a) shall include information about—

paragraph.text: any tools and resources the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation and the National Credit Union Administration would need to effectively implement the standard maximum deposit insurance amount determined appropriate by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation and the National Credit Union Administration;

the benefits that would be associated with implementing the standard maximum deposit insurance amount determined appropriate by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation and the National Credit Union Administration; and

any operational or administrative protocols the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation and the National Credit Union Administration would need to establish to implement and administer the standard maximum deposit insurance amount determined appropriate by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation and the National Credit Union Administration, including protocols for the annual adjustment described under section 11(a)(1)(F) of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act.
